index.04: I Gift Aid turns urgent needs into daily gifts. We simplify giving with fair exposure for every campaign, a Daily Needs Wall, and faster, cheaper payouts to the people who need them.
index.05: Our mission is simple: a regular and fair flow of donations to the most in-need, every day.
index.08: A verified family raising for one large need — treatment, rebuilding, a year of school. Each will run for weeks on a regulated fundraising platform.
index.11: One small, specific thing a family needs this week — usually $18 to $100. Posted once a day, gone in 24 hours. You will be able to pick several and settle them together.
index.12: Neither is ranked by popularity. Campaigns are shuffled on every visit and the wall shows whatever expires soonest, so a family who has raised nothing is as visible as one who has nearly finished. That is what fair exposure means here.
index.14: I Gift Aid is the name we operate under. HEART Humanitarian Foundation is the charity behind it — a nonprofit corporation registered in Pennsylvania and recognised by the Internal Revenue Service as a 501(c)(3) tax-exempt public charity. They are one organisation, not two: HEART is doing business as I Gift Aid.
index.15: Every donation is made to HEART Humanitarian Foundation. You can verify our status independently with the IRS using our EIN, 42‑2670441, at irs.gov.
index.18: Our campaigns are hosted and operated on regulated fundraising platforms; these partners handle donor processing, compliance, and disbursement. We coordinate and curate, the platforms below provide the regulated rails.
index.28: Applying for support, or asking about a campaign? Message us on WhatsApp — it reaches our team directly, in English or Arabic.
index.30: Partners, beneficiaries and donors can also reach us at hello@igiftaid.org.
how-it-works.01: What happens between you giving and a family receiving — including the parts that are still imperfect.
how-it-works.02: Most giving platforms show you a story and a progress bar. That tells you nothing about whether the person is real, or whether the money arrives. This page is what happens between you giving and a family receiving — including the parts that are still imperfect.
how-it-works.05: Almost always on WhatsApp, in Arabic, from a phone. They tell us who is in the household, what has happened, what they need, and how money could reach them. It is free and it always will be.
how-it-works.07: Identity documents, photographs taken by them rather than found online, and a wallet or account that matches the person we verified. Applications that cannot be verified do not become campaigns.
how-it-works.09: Before any money moves, the recipient is screened against sanctions lists. HEART is a US charity and cannot lawfully send funds to a sanctioned person, entity or jurisdiction — and does not.
how-it-works.11: We write it with the family, using their own words and their own photographs. It goes onto a regulated fundraising platform — Chuffed or GoFundMe — which handles the donor payment under its own compliance regime.
how-it-works.13: Your donation is made to HEART Humanitarian Foundation, which operates as I Gift Aid. It becomes the charity's property on receipt, and we apply it to the cause you gave to.
how-it-works.14: The money is sent, and recorded
how-it-works.15: Funds reach the family by the route that actually works where they are — often a digital wallet rather than a bank. Every transfer is recorded against the campaign it came from.
how-it-works.17: Two deductions happen to your donation, and we would rather name them separately than quote one number that hides the other.
how-it-works.19: Taken by Chuffed, GoFundMe, Stripe or PayPal before the money reaches us. Typically around 2.5% plus a fixed amount per donation. We never see it and we cannot waive it.
how-it-works.21: Applied to what actually arrives. It covers currency exchange, the cost of moving money into a place where ordinary banking does not work, and running the charity. It is a range because those costs genuinely vary per transfer. It is cost recovery, not profit.
how-it-works.22: Where we are honest about the limits
how-it-works.23: We identify and promote the families we raise for, and we verify who they are. We do not claim more than we do. Where a campaign has had a specific check, the campaign says which. Where it has not, it does not pretend otherwise.
how-it-works.24: Approving an application is not a promise that it will raise anything. Some campaigns fund in days and some never fund. We tell families that before they start, because the alternative is raising hope we cannot deliver.
how-it-works.25: We can be wrong. If you believe a campaign on this site is not what it says it is, tell us at hello@igiftaid.org. We would rather take something down and apologise than leave it up and hope.
trust.02: Everything here can be verified with a government registry, without asking us.
trust.03: You should not have to take our word for any of this. Everything below can be checked by you, with a government registry, without asking us.
trust.06: Search our EIN, 42‑2670441, in the IRS Tax Exempt Organization Search. It will confirm we are a 501(c)(3) public charity in good standing and that donations are deductible.
trust.09: We hold Certificate of Registration 124454 from the Bureau of Corporations and Charitable Organizations, which is the state's permission to solicit donations at all — a separate thing from tax exemption.
trust.11: I Gift Aid is the trading name of HEART Humanitarian Foundation — one organisation, two names. HEART is a Pennsylvania nonprofit corporation and a registered 501(c)(3) public charity. As a nonstock corporation it has no members and no shareholders: nobody owns it, and no individual can take profit from it. Its directors are named on the HEART website.
trust.13: We never charge a family anything. Not to apply, not to be prioritised, not to receive funds. If someone contacts you asking for payment in our name, they are not us — please tell us.
trust.14: We do not rank by popularity, and nothing can be paid for. There is no featured slot on this site and no way to buy one. Campaigns are shuffled on every visit; the Daily Needs Wall defaults to whatever expires soonest.
trust.15: We do not send funds where we may not. Recipients are screened against sanctions lists before money moves. This occasionally means declining a family we would want to help.
trust.16: We do not claim UK Gift Aid. Our name says “Gift Aid” and people reasonably ask. Gift Aid is a UK relief needing an HMRC-recognised charity; HEART is American, so it is not available on any donation here. US donors do get a genuine deduction under section 170.
trust.18: Donations are processed by regulated payment platforms, not by us — we never see or store your card details. Our privacy policy sets out what we do hold and for how long, and you can ask us to delete it at any time via our data deletion page. This site runs no analytics, no advertising trackers and no profiling cookies.
